images.caption: Figure 1:(a–c) PhysInsert simultaneously supports cross-environment adaptation, bidirectional object–scene interactions, and cross-view adaptation. (d) InsertWorld offers broad coverage of scenes, object properties, and interaction types.
Figure 2:Overview of InsertWorld construction and PhysInsert-Bench composition.

Figure 3:PhysInsert combines a VGGT geometry stream with image and text streams. Target-scene features supervise geometry-token states, while 2D-OSS aligns object/effect predictions and spatial-text attention with image regions. Auxiliary supervision is used only during training.
Figure 5:Qualitative comparisons on PhysInsert-Bench (top), DreamBooth and PhysInsert-Bench-Wild (middle), and the user-study set (bottom).

Figure 6:Mechanism probes and qualitative ablations. (a) Spatial-text attention, object/effect predictions, and VGGT feature evolution under identical GT-noised inputs (σ=0.5\sigma=0.5). (b) Separate ablations of SSG, GGA, and COSS for placement and scale, perspective, and floor reflection. (c) Text-guided pose and placement control.

header: Appendix for PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions

images.caption: Figure S1:Selected box-guided comparisons on PhysInsert-Bench with one reference image. DIRECT additionally receives GT pose.
Figure S2:Selected text-guided comparisons on PhysInsert-Bench with one reference image. References are center-cropped only for visualization.

Figure S3:Additional qualitative comparisons on DreamBooth (1/2). Columns show the background, object reference, ground-truth target (GT), OmniPaint, InsertAnything, DIRECT, GPT-Image2, Nano Banana Pro, and Ours. DIRECT uses a GT-pose RGB proxy; GPT-Image2 and Nano Banana Pro use text guidance.
Figure S4:Additional qualitative comparisons on DreamBooth (2/2). The column order and method settings are the same as in FigureS3.

Figure S5:Additional qualitative comparisons on 11 cases from the in-the-wild user-study set. Columns show the object reference, background scene, OmniPaint, InsertAnything, DIRECT, Nano Banana Pro, and Ours. White boxes in the scene column indicate approximate insertion regions. OmniPaint is included for qualitative comparison only and was not part of the user-study ratings.

Figure S6:Five InsertWorld training examples. Each row contains the with-object scene (With), the corresponding object-free scene (Without), and the isolated target rendered from the scene viewpoint on a white display background (Removed-only). The right panel shows the same target under two lighting conditions (rows L1 and L2) and four corresponding fixed viewpoints (columns). Lighting conditions and viewpoints are selected separately for each example.

Figure S7:PhysInsert-Bench samples (1/4). The original interaction tag appears at left in readable form, followed by the object-free scene (Without), with-object target (GT), and actual single-view object input. Case IDs refer to the benchmark manifest.

Figure S8:PhysInsert-Bench samples (2/4). Column meanings follow FigureS7. The reference is the actual one-view benchmark input, including its original background; it is neither a multiview collage nor a newly rendered reference.

Figure S9:PhysInsert-Bench samples (3/4). Column meanings follow FigureS7. The examples illustrate cloth, suspension, leaning, flat support, and depth ordering using the original benchmark annotations.

Figure S10:PhysInsert-Bench samples (4/4). Column meanings follow FigureS7. These examples cover partial occlusion, placement relations, scale adaptation, perspective foreshortening, and viewpoint gaps.
